title: Per-shard admission SLI + progressive multi-region failover storyboard & dashboard
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Implement per-shard admission-controller SLIs and a progressive multi-region failover storyboard tied to a Grafana dashboard bundle. Rationale: current region-level SLOs obscure shard-level admission anomalies that precede token latency spikes and cascade into cross-region failovers. This ticket delivers metric instrumentation, dashboard panels, alert rules, and a documented canary playbook to enable safer progressive rollouts and automated soft-circuit decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Per-shard metrics emitted: admit_rate, admit_latency_p50/p95/p99 (ms), queue_depth, shed_rate, kv_prefix_hit_ratio
Dashboard with per-region + per-shard panels, heatmap for shed_rate and p99 admit_latency, and merged view for on-call
Alerting rules: early-warning (admit_latency_p95 > threshold), pre-shed (queue_depth growth + kv_hit_drop), and emergency-shed trigger
Canary storyboard: documented step-by-step failover/unwind scenario and automation hooks for progressive region spillover
Load test synthetic demonstrating SLI sensitivity and dashboard fidelity (load harness PR merged)
Documentation: Confluence runbook + links to GitHub PRs and Grafana dashboard JSON in repo
implementation_notes: Instrumentation: add per-shard labels to admission metrics emitted by the admission-controller (shard_id, region, pool_type). Use aggregated histograms with configurable bucket boundaries to reduce cardinality cost; export p50/p95/p99 via Prometheus recording rules. For token-level latency, capture admit-to-dispatch latency and a separate per-token KV prefix-hit metric. In Grafana, use Loki traces to link outlier p99s to sampled spans (one in 1000) to keep tracing costs manageable. Trade-offs: higher cardinality provides faster detection of noisy shards but increases Prometheus TSDB costs — mitigate with downsampling and cardinality caps. Circuit behavior: implement soft-circuit state with hysteresis based on rolling-window shed_rate and p99 latency, enable automatic progressive shedding only when synthetic canary gates (synthetic traffic checks) pass.
